Ad Lugdunénse concílium a beáto Gregório: Summoned to the Council of Lyons by blessed Gregory the Tenth and created Cardinal Bishop of Albano, he rendered distinguished service in the weighty affairs of the Council, whereby the dissensions of the schism were composed and the doctrines of the Church vindicated. In the midst of these labours, in the fifty-third year of his age and the year of salvation twelve hundred and seventy-four, he died, to the deep sorrow of all, and was honoured at his funeral by the whole Council, the Roman Pontiff himself being present. Sixtus the Fourth enrolled him, renowned for very many and very great miracles, in the number of the Saints. He wrote much, and in his writings, joining the highest learning with the ardour of piety, he moves the reader while he teaches him: wherefore Sixtus the Fifth deservedly honoured him with the title of the Seraphic Doctor.
Benedicite Dómino, omnes virtútes ejus:: Bless the Lord, all ye His hosts: ye His ministers, that do His will. Alleluia.

Cum autem illud ex Evangélio audísset: N: But when he had heard that saying of the Gospel: Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money in your purses, nor scrip for your journey, nor two coats, nor shoes, he set it before himself as a rule to be kept. And so, putting off his shoes and content with one tunic, having taken to himself twelve companions, he founded the Order of Friars Minor. Wherefore he came to Rome in the year of salvation twelve hundred and nine, that the rule of his Order might be confirmed by the Apostolic See. The Supreme Pontiff Innocent the Third at first rejected him as he approached; but because afterwards in his sleep he seemed to see the man whom he had repulsed holding up on his shoulders the Lateran basilica as it was falling, he had him sought out and sent for, and, receiving him kindly, confirmed the whole plan of his institute. Francis then, having sent his brethren into all parts of the world to preach the Gospel of Christ, and himself desiring that some occasion of martyrdom might be given him, sailed into Syria; where, being treated most generously by the Sultan, and accomplishing nothing, he returned to Italy.
Deus, qui Beátum Sigismúndum Regem utróq: O God, who were pleased to honour blessed Sigismund the King with both crowns, the temporal and the eternal, together with the palm he longed for, and revealed his relics from the depths of the waters for the faithful to venerate: grant, we beseech You, that we who venerate his merits may by his intercession be protected from all adversities.

Dóminus secus mare Galilǽæ vidit duos fr: The Lord, by the sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Peter and Andrew, and He called them: Come ye after Me: I will make you to be fishers of men.
Ego pascam oves meas: et ego eas accubár: I will feed My sheep: and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God. I will seek that which was lost: and that which was driven away I will bring again: and I will bind up that which was broken, and I will strengthen that which was weak.
Eo quod liberássem páuperem vociferántem: Because I had delivered the poor man that cried out, and the fatherless that had no helper, the blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me, and I comforted the heart of the widow: I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame: I was the father of the poor.
Hujus sacrifícii poténtia, Dómine, quǽsu: May the power of this sacrifice, O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully cleanse away our old life, and increase in us newness of life and salvation.
Hæc dicit Dóminus: Dissólve colligatióne: Thus saith the Lord: Loose the bands of wickedness, undo the bundles that oppress, let them that are broken go free, and break asunder every burden. Deal thy bread to the hungry, and bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house: when thou shalt see one naked, cover him, and despise not thy own flesh. Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thy health shall speedily arise, and thy justice shall go before thy face, and the glory of the Lord shall gather thee up. Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall hear: thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. When thou shalt pour out thy soul to the hungry, and shalt satisfy the afflicted soul, then shall thy light rise up in darkness, and thy darkness shall be as the noonday.

In illo témpore: Legisperítus quidam, vo: At that time, a certain lawyer, willing to justify himself, said to Jesus: And who is my neighbour? And Jesus answering, said: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers, who also stripped him, and having wounded him went away, leaving him half dead. And it chanced that a certain priest went down the same way: and seeing him, passed by. In like manner also a Levite, when he was near the place and saw him, passed by. But a certain Samaritan being on his journey, came near him: and seeing him, was moved with compassion. And going up to him, bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine: and setting him upon his own beast, brought him to an inn, and took care of him. And the next day he took out two pence, and gave to the host, and said: Take care of him; and whatsoever thou shalt spend over and above, I, at my return, will repay thee. Which of these three, in thy opinion, was neighbour to him that fell among the robbers? But he said: He that shewed mercy to him. And Jesus said to him: Go, and do thou in like manner.
In illo témpore: Vidit Jesus publicánum: At that time, Jesus saw a publican named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom, and He said to him: Follow Me. And leaving all things, he rose up and followed Him. And Levi made Him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans, and of others, that were at table with them. But the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying to His disciples: Why do you eat and drink with publicans and sinners? And Jesus answering, said to them: They that are whole need not the physician, but they that are sick. I came not to call the just, but sinners to penance.
Liberábit páuperem a poténte, et páupere: He shall deliver the poor from the mighty, and the needy that had no helper: He shall spare the poor and needy, and He shall save the souls of the poor.

Huc accedit quod dicitur fuísse de domo: To this is added that he is said to have been of the house of David. For truly of the house of David, truly of royal stock, does this man Joseph descend, noble in birth, nobler still in mind: plainly a son of David, not unworthy of his father David.
Jacob autem genuit Joseph. Hunc locum ob: And Jacob begot Joseph. This passage Julian the Emperor cast up against us as a disagreement of the Evangelists: why the Evangelist Matthew called Joseph the son of Jacob, while Luke called him the son of Heli; not understanding the custom of the Scriptures, that one was his father by nature, the other by the law. For we know that this was commanded through Moses at the bidding of God, that if a brother or kinsman died without children, another should take his wife to raise up seed to his brother or kinsman. Joseph the husband of Mary. When you hear husband, let no suspicion of wedlock arise in you; but remember the custom of the Scriptures, that the betrothed are called husbands and the betrothed wives.
Et a transmigratione Babylonis usque ad: And from the transmigration of Babylon to Christ are fourteen generations. Count from Jechonias to Joseph, and you will find thirteen generations; the fourteenth generation, therefore, will be reckoned in Christ Himself. Now the generation of Christ was in this wise. The careful reader may ask and say: Since Joseph is not the father of the Lord the Saviour, what has the line of the generation brought down to Joseph to do with the Lord? To whom we shall answer, first, that it is not the custom of the Scriptures that a line of women be woven into a generation; and next, that Joseph and Mary were of one tribe, whence by the law he was bound to take her as his kinswoman:
